primitives.name: Throwing trajectory optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: 210 WALTER CAMP'S BOOK OF COLLEGE SPORTS almost no chance to recover and put the ball on the man, whereas a low throw brings his hands in the most advantageous position for touching the runner.
primitives.assumptions: Constant gravitational acceleration, negligible air resistance, rigid body mechanics of arm and hand.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ball velocity drops below threshold requiring recovery time exceeding defensive window.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI optimal Bayesian shot selection under uncertainty, where high-risk throws (e.g., overthrows) increase error variance.
layer2.telemetry: Throw velocity, release angle, and receiver reaction time.

primitives.name: Catcher throw efficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: The same is, of course, true in the case of the catcher's throws to the second or the other bases, to put out the runner.
primitives.assumptions: Uniform distribution of runner advance probabilities across all bases, constant pop-time for catcher.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Pop-time exceeds runner's base-running speed multiplied by distance.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE state-transition models where catcher-to-base transitions determine double-play success rates.
layer2.telemetry: Pop-time, runner's sprint speed, and throw accuracy metrics.

primitives.name: Finger position control
primitives.verbatim_quote: The position of the fingers when throwing a ball is a point upon which there are individual differences of opinion; but the majority of the best throwers in the country use principally the fore-finger and middlefinger in giving direction to the ball.
primitives.assumptions: Fixed grip stiffness, linear relationship between finger pressure and spin rate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inconsistent grip leads to unpredictable spin axis and reduced aerodynamic stability.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI conformal prediction intervals for spin rate and velocity, accounting for player-specific biomechanical variability.
layer2.telemetry: Spin rate, release velocity, and grip configuration data.

primitives.name: Handling accuracy
primitives.verbatim_quote: Handling the ball well is quite as important an element in the game as throwing.
primitives.assumptions: Perfectly elastic collision between glove and ball, zero deflection angle.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ball leaves glove at non-zero angle relative to intended catch trajectory.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE event tagging algorithms that classify catches as 'secure' versus 'fumble', affecting subsequent play states.
layer2.telemetry: Catch probability scores derived from ball exit velocity and glove movement vectors.
